_about: Morvane's spoken lines (hand-written; ElevenLabs only reads them). Source of truth for tools/install_voices.py, which writes scripts/lore/data/morvane_lines.js and installs the picked takes. fx: far = before the Rift (filtered, distant), mid = in the Hollow, dry = in the fight. The fight lines (act 'The fight') are voiced without the player's name; their chat text stays in lore/data/reveal.js and bestiary/morvane.js.

voice.description: A man who sounds about sixty but is far older, once a king, worn thin by centuries alone underground. Low, quiet, grave baritone with a little hoarseness, very calm and courteous, old-fashioned precise English with a received pronunciation accent softened by tiredness. Never raises his voice; speaks close and unhurried, as if from just behind you in the dark, with sorrow and patience under the authority.

lines.when: Your first dusk in the world, once.
lines.text: You do not remember packing it. That is all right. Read it when you cannot sleep.
lines.why: Echoes the journal's first line. The last page ends: You did not pack this book. I did.

lines.when: The first time you finish the Old King's Journal.
lines.text: He wrote that last line for his son. His son listened. Nobody else did.
lines.why: The last page: I did what his last line told me. I listened before I rang.

lines.when: Dusk of your first siege night.
lines.text: Third night. Light your lamps; they come for the brightest. I am sorry. It was agreed long before you.
lines.why: He runs the sieges, and the truce gave the third night away.

lines.when: The morning after your first siege is held.
lines.text: Well held. They will remember your walls now. So will I.
lines.why: He taught the Hollow our walls.

lines.when: When the Ember falls near your keep.
lines.text: Careful with that. I held one once, and the hand never closed again.
lines.why: He took the Crown's splinter in his right hand and fights left-handed.

lines.when: The first time you bring down the Warlord King.
lines.text: Up you get, Vorlund. They are not finished with you. Neither am I.
lines.why: Vorlund's Ledger clue: I have never seen him. I know the voice.

lines.when: When the Clockwork Reeve falls.
lines.text: Seventeen minutes past three. I remember that minute too. Let it go now.
lines.why: The Grey Host was taken at 3:17, under his truce.

lines.when: When the Pale Huntsman falls.
lines.text: He walked off the ice alone and never forgave it for letting him. I know the feeling.
lines.why: He walked into the Hollow alone, upright.

lines.when: When the Drowned Bride falls.
lines.text: Someone up there still writes to her. Three hundred years, and nobody ever wrote to me.
lines.why: The Order erased him; no portrait, no grave.

lines.when: When the Ash Seneschal falls.
lines.text: He kept my keys a long time. Longer than I asked him to.
lines.why: A seneschal keeps his lord's keys. The statues show the king's life.

lines.when: When the Mother of Changelings falls.
lines.text: She would kill to keep her name. I should have liked the chance.
lines.why: His name was burned; the Hollow made him a new one.

lines.act: Third nights (each once, now and then)
lines.when: Faint, inside the singing on a third night.
lines.text: Every third night. Somebody has to knock.
lines.why: I knocked on it every third night for three hundred years.

lines.act: Third nights (each once, now and then)
lines.when: Faint, inside the singing on a third night.
lines.text: Your bells are louder than ours were. Ours were better made.

lines.act: Third nights (each once, now and then)
lines.when: Faint, inside the singing on a third night.
lines.text: Somebody up there is ringing too soon. Listen first.

lines.act: Third nights (each once, now and then)
lines.when: Faint, inside the singing on a third night.
lines.text: It was never the dark you ought to fear. It was the quiet after.

lines.act: Third nights (each once, now and then)
lines.when: Faint, inside the singing on a third night.
lines.text: You sleep with your boots on now. Good.

lines.act: Third nights (each once, now and then)
lines.when: Faint, inside the singing on a third night.
lines.text: I used to count the nights. Then I counted the bells. Now I only listen.

lines.act: Third nights (each once, now and then)
lines.when: Faint, inside the singing on a third night.
lines.text: Mind the wells. Water goes down, and it remembers the way.
lines.why: Corvin's ashes went into running water, and water runs down.

lines.act: Third nights (each once, now and then)
lines.when: Faint, inside the singing on a third night.
lines.text: My father heard this too. He thought it was the wind.
lines.why: Aldric's journal: singing under the floor every third night.

lines.when: When you strike the Tuning Fork and the Rift opens.
lines.text: There. You found the door. I knocked on it for a very long time.

lines.when: Your first steps in the Hollow.
lines.text: Come down, then. Mind the light. It runs downhill here, like everything else.

lines.when: When the Choir is silenced.
lines.text: You stopped their singing. It is very quiet without it. Come up. I have kept the chair.
lines.why: Stage 6: There is only the one chair.

lines.when: He rises from the Seat. The first time you see who has been talking.
lines.text: Sit, then. If you can take it from me.

lines.when: Stage 4, under your own sky gone the wrong colour.
lines.text: This was mine first.

lines.when: Stage 4 breaks and the ground takes you back down.
lines.text: Not here. Not under this sky.

lines.when: Stage 6, the Fall: alone with him.
lines.text: Sit, if you like. There is only the one chair, and I have had it three hundred years.

lines.when: Stage 6.
lines.text: I was a king. Yours. Your walls stand on my roads. Did nobody up there tell you there had been one?

lines.when: Stage 6.
lines.text: I made a peace, and I kept it. I am the only one on either side of that door who did.

lines.when: Stage 6.
lines.text: There is no portrait of me left above. Forty-one, and she burned them all. You would not have known my face. You have known my nights.

lines.when: Stage 6.
lines.text: Tell my daughter the door was well made. Tell her I knocked every third night.

lines.when: Stage 6 breaks.
lines.text: Good. You did not come down here to talk either.

lines.when: The reveal: the boy at the desk ages into him and looks up. The only spoken line in the scene.
lines.text: You kept my father's book.

lines.when: New: as he falls for good.
lines.text: Listen before you ring.
lines.why: The journal's last line, and the last line of his own page.
